description: 2043 is the Year of the Water Pig in the Chinese zodiac, from February 10, 2043 to January 29, 2044. Personality, Lunar New Year dates and numerology.
answer: In Chinese astrology, 2043 is the Year of the Water Pig, a Yin year. It began at Lunar New Year on February 10, 2043 and ended on January 29, 2044, so people born in 2043 before Feb 10 belong to the Water Dog year.

sections.heading: 2043 Lunar New Year: start and end dates
paragraphs: Lunar New Year opened the Water Pig year on February 10, 2043, and the year ran to January 29, 2044. So a birth date of Feb 10, 2043 or later counts as Water Pig, and so do early 2044 birthdays through Jan 29; births in 2043 before Feb 10 still belong to the Water Dog. That moving boundary comes from the lunisolar calendar, in which the new year starts with the second new moon after the winter solstice in most years, so its Gregorian date shifts by up to a month from one year to the next. Look sixty years either side and the pairing repeats: 1983 are Water Pig years too. That Tuesday new year arrived with the Sun in Aquarius in the Western zodiac.

sections.heading: What the Water Pig is like
paragraphs: Double Water gives this Pig year a reputation for warmth and peacefulness. Those born now are pictured as sensitive, generous and reluctant to fight. They make cherished friends. Saying no kindly but clearly, setting deadlines for decisions and raising small concerns early protect their open hearts and keep life from drifting. Their homes tend to be welcoming, unhurried places where friends feel free to linger.

In classical thought, Water belongs to the north and to the deep, resting energy of winter, the season when life gathers strength out of sight. As a year stem, it tends to make an animal more reflective, adaptable and emotionally attuned. People born under a Water stem are often described as clever negotiators, sensitive friends and natural mediators who prefer influence to force. They value understanding and tend to think before they act. The caution traditionally attached to Water is fluidity taken too far: avoiding conflict, keeping too much hidden and losing a clear sense of their own direction.

sections.heading: 2043 in the animal cycle and in numerology
paragraphs: In numerology the year reduces to 9, the number of completion, generosity and letting go, and a 9 year is traditionally read as one of endings that clear space. The digits of 2043 add up to 9. The Pig holds the twelfth place among the twelve animals and its fixed element is Water. Set beside the year's Water stem, water year element matches the fixed element, which readings use to describe how settled or stretched the combination feels. The year before was the Water Dog and the year after is the Wood Rat.

Chinese almanacs name 2043 Gui-Hai, pairing the Water stem Gui with the branch Hai. Both are Yin, as stem and branch always share a polarity, so of the hundred and twenty possible pairings only sixty ever occur, and each one names a single year in every cycle.

faq.question: What Chinese zodiac is 2043?
faq.answer: 2043 is the Year of the Water Pig. It started on February 10, 2043 and ended on January 29, 2044.

faq.question: What if I was born in January or February 2043?
faq.answer: Check the date against Feb 10. Born before February 10, 2043, you are a Water Dog; born on or after it, you are a Water Pig.

faq.question: What element is 2043 in the Chinese zodiac?
faq.answer: Water, a Yin year. The Pig's own fixed element is Water; the year element changes every two years, while the fixed element stays with the animal.

faq.question: What is the traditional Chinese name for 2043?
faq.answer: Gui-Hai. The first part is the heavenly stem, which carries the year's element and polarity; the second is the earthly branch, which carries the animal. Almanacs, calendars and Four Pillars charts identify years this way rather than by animal alone.

faq.question: When is the next Water Pig year?
faq.answer: 2103, sixty years later, when the five elements and twelve animals line up again; the table also has 1983.
